results.evidence: slack_settings.py: `if not stored: return None` in get_untagged_followup_preference, and resolve_untagged_followup_mode does `return preference if preference is not None else UntaggedFollowupMode.ASK`. So no row or an empty column now resolves to ASK, and messaging.py's activity reaches `_post_untagged_followup_prompt(...)` instead of the NEVER branch.

An explicitly stored valid value is returned unchanged (`if stored in UntaggedFollowupMode.values: return UntaggedFollowupMode(stored)`). The activity still does `if mode == AUTO: return False` and `if mode == NEVER: ... return True`, and ASK prompts. Explicit choices take the same paths as before.

The default-saving row only appears when `offer_default = (slack_user_id == mapping.mentioning_slack_user_id and get_untagged_followup_preference(...) is None)`. Any replier who isn't the thread creator, and a creator who explicitly chose ask, gets only 'Yes, take a look' / 'No thanks', with no way to record a default. `_save_untagged_followup_default` also returns early `if not context.get("offer_default")`. The prompt shown to the replier does not generally offer a default choice.

_build_home_view passes `untagged_followup_mode=resolve_untagged_followup_mode(integration, slack_user_id)`, which is now ASK for unset users. Because it is not None, render_home_view adds `_untagged_followups_section_blocks(untagged_followup_mode)` with `initial_option` matching `mode.value` ('Ask them first'). The picker saves via save_untagged_followup_mode.
get_untagged_followup_preference: after the valid-value check it ends with `return UntaggedFollowupMode.NEVER` for an unrecognised stored value, so resolve returns NEVER rather than ASK.

The only pointer is plain text: "You can change it any time under *Thread follow-ups* on my Home tab." No link is built, even though `app_home_url` is imported in api.py, and there is no linked/unlinked fallback. The note is also only added `if offer_default:`.

The patch has no AI credits quota logic. No visible code stops unconfirmed untagged replies silently while still posting the denial for mentions and confirmed replies. The only related code is the existing `untagged_followup_confirmed=True` passed to `_start_mention_workflow`, and nothing in the diff ties it to quota handling.

result:
People who never chose a thread follow-up setting now get asked about untagged replies instead of having them silently ignored. If the person replying started the thread, the prompt also lets them save a default. People who already chose a setting see no change. Per your instructions I didn't run the tests. The changed files compile, but ruff isn't installed here, so nothing was formatted or linted.

**What changed**

- **No setting now means "ask".** The setting is read from the person who started the thread. In `products/slack_app/backend/services/slack_settings.py`, a missing or empty setting now counts as "Ask before picking it up" instead of "Never". Two cases still count as "Never": a thread whose starter is unknown, and an old stored value the code no longer recognises. I added two small helpers: one that tells "never chose" apart from an actual choice, and one that saves a choice.
- **The prompt can save a default.** In `messaging.py` and `api.py`, when the thread starter never chose a setting and is the one replying, the private yes/no prompt gets a second row: **"Always pick up follow-ups"** and **"Never pick up follow-ups"**. "Always" sends this reply and saves "always"; "Never" drops it and saves "never". A note under the buttons says the setting can be changed any time under *Thread follow-ups* on the Home tab. A save only happens if that prompt actually offered the buttons and the person clicking is the one it was sent to.
- **Home tab.** The *Thread follow-ups* picker was already on the Home tab. People with no setting now see "Ask them first" selected, which matches what actually happens. The picker saves through the same helper as the prompt, and I updated the outdated comments.

**Decision for you:** only the thread starter is offered the save buttons. Their setting decides every reply in their threads, so a save from anyone else would never stop the prompts in that thread. As a result, other people replying in a thread whose starter hasn't chosen get the plain yes/no prompt every time. If you'd rather everyone could set a default, the setting would have to start depending on the replier, which is a bigger change to how it works.

**Tests**

- Updated the existing tests that expected "no setting" to mean "never": the settings test now expects "ask", and the routing test now expects the reply to be sent on.
- Added tests for:
  - saving and reading back a setting;
  - which prompts offer the save buttons (the thread starter with no setting gets them; anyone else, or someone who already chose, doesn't);
  - "Always" sending the reply and saving "always", and "Never" dropping it and saving "never";
  - the buttons saving nothing on a prompt that didn't offer them.
